consensus_summary: No single settled symbolic meaning; most often a complete or divinely appointed period/cycle/season of time (especially Jubilee or 'year of the Lord's favor' as era of salvation/release), with common alternatives in prophetic day-year scaling, 360-day apocalyptic years, divine-vs-human time, or judgment periods.
book_summary: A turning (Hebrew shanah: change/repeat/return); one complete cycle of time at whatever scale the count is running, illustrated by Jeremiah’s seventy years closing only as seventy jubilees and a thousand years passing as a day.
consensus_core_identification: A complete or divinely appointed cycle/period/season of time (context-dependent; frequently the Jubilee/'acceptable year' of favor and restoration).
book_core_identification: One complete cycle of time (etymologically a turning/repetition), scalable to any level of the count.
boundary_disagreement: Book explicitly generalizes the cycle to arbitrary scales and reclassifies Jeremiah’s seventy years as seventy jubilees (plus the day=thousand-years equivalence), admitting multi-scale and specific long-range prophetic mappings that consensus treats only as secondary alternatives or leaves context-bound.
rationale: Both cores reduce to the same minimal referent (a complete cycle/period of time). Consensus already lists 'complete cycle' language and the cited scalings (Jubilee, day-year, Ps 90:4) among primaries or alternatives; the book keeps that referent while broadening its extension and precision via the root and scale-invariance, without replacing the central identification. Hence REFINED rather than MATCH (material boundary shift) or DIVERGENT/NOVEL (no contradiction or absence).
strongest_objection: Consensus primaries foreground the soteriological 'year of the Lord'/Jubilee era of favor, which the book entry neither states nor prioritizes, treating the term more etymologically and chronographically.
